text: Giovanni Baschenis (1471–1503) was an Italian painter whose name is often combined with that of his brother Battista, who was also a painter. Giovanni was the son of Antonio from the Lanfranco family and the nephew of Angelo. Some of Giovanni’s paintings are associated with Battista, who likely served as the sole assistant. Giovanni began his artistic career in Trentino with his brother, but after returning to Bergamo, he continued working independently. In Trentino, the two brothers collaborated on frescoes for the chapel of San Valerio in Castel Valer in Tassullo, the Church of Santi Filippo and Giacomo in Segonzone (in the municipality of Campodenno), and the church of Sant'Udalrico in Corte Inferiore (Noise) in Val di Non; the 1471 fresco of the 'Last Supper' bears the inscription Joha[n]nes et Baptista de Averaria pinxeru[n]t 1471. Giovanni returned to his homeland, Bergamo, where he frescoed the Casa Volpi in Fuipiano al Brembo. The fresco of Christ on the tomb between Mary and John includes the inscription Ritius filius quodam Zani hoc opus fieri and die 4 novembris 1486 in the upper part, depicting a red tomb with Christ supported by the Mother on the right and Saint John praying on the left; the upper section contains a long inscription providing instructions for obtaining an indulgence, which contains an error in stating the indulgence spans twenty-two thousand years. At the bottom, he signs Johannes de Avaia pixit. A second fresco, the Madonna and Child among the Saints, lacks the plasticity characteristic of Renaissance art, though the Madonna’s cloak with printed flowers adds solemnity. In the sacristy of the church in the Alino hamlet of San Pellegrino Terme, there is a fresco signed and dated 1478 depicting the Original Sin, showing Eve covering herself with the apple in her hand and revealing her nakedness, and Adam touching his throat as if to feel the Adam's apple grow; another fresco, the Theory of the Saints, depicts five saints—John the Baptist, Saint Blaise, Mary Magdalene, Saint Defendente, and the central figure of Saint Catherine of Alexandria being crowned by two angels—and is dated 1470, attributed to Giovanni Baschenis by Luigi Angelini. Frescoes of San Defendente in the apse of the Church of San Defendente in Roncola date to 1482, and in 1490 Giovanni frescoed the church of San Lorenzo in Cunevo.
